memories.content: The user stores copies of identity documents in an encrypted folder.
On a day the user transferred between buses twice, they rested for an hour after the trip.
On a day the user took a direct route with a similar travel time, they remained seated to the destination.
After arriving at an entrance with stairs only, the user went around to an entrance on the other side of the building.
On a day the user checked the accessible entrance location in advance, they arrived before the agreed time.
On a rainy day, the user's clothes became wet while crossing an uncovered section at a transfer stop.
On a day the user traveled with their maternal uncle, they agreed to meet at an entrance near the elevator.
The user's maternal uncle prefers an aisle seat from which it is easy to stand during long-distance travel.
The local agent cannot know whether an accessible entrance is operating that day from past route records alone.
The transfer route the user takes has more boarding and alighting events and walking segments than the direct route.
One of the user's identity documents needs renewal in the second half of 2025.
The user postponed an application until the next day after spending time looking for document photos in scattered folders.
After gathering the necessary copies in one folder, the user completed the renewal form in one sitting.
The user entered an abbreviated name on an official form and then discovered that it differed from the supporting document.
On the next application, after comparing the name with the source document, the user did not receive a correction request.
The user put only the submission deadline in the calendar and missed the application deadline by one day because they did not check the issuance period.
On the next application, the user recorded the expected issuance date separately in the calendar.
Staff at a public-service counter expect a person requesting identity verification to bring an original as well as a copy.
When planning an official application, put both the submission deadline and expected issuance date in the calendar and verify them.
The local agent cannot determine the current validity of an identity document without its expiration date.

analysis.overview: The frames overlap on organizing identity-document copies but otherwise contribute separate evidence: the reference emphasizes travel and accessibility experiences, while the compared frame covers application preparation, form accuracy, scheduling, verification requirements, renewal timing, and document-validity limits.

relations.reason: The reference describes copies stored together securely; the compared memories describe scattered files delaying an application and consolidation enabling completion. These claims materially address document-copy organization and can jointly govern it.
relations.summary: Consolidating identity-document copies supports efficient retrieval, while encrypted storage adds a compatible security property.

relations.reason: These reference memories collectively split one comparative account of how transfer-heavy and direct routes differ in movement demands and observed travel experience; the compared frame contains no corresponding route claim.
relations.summary: Transfer travel involved additional boarding, alighting, and walking demands and was followed by rest, whereas comparable direct travel allowed continuous seating.

relations.reason: This is a one-sided observation about an accessibility-related navigation response, with no corresponding application or document-management claim in the compared frame.
relations.summary: A stairs-only entrance caused the user to detour to another side of the building.

relations.reason: This independently useful reference-side observation concerns advance accessibility planning and arrival timing; the compared frame does not address it.
relations.summary: Checking the accessible entrance location in advance coincided with arriving before the agreed time.

relations.reason: This reference-only claim records a weather-related transfer-route consequence not addressed by the compared frame.
relations.summary: An uncovered transfer-stop section exposed the user to rain and wet clothing.

relations.reason: This is a reference-only travel coordination detail involving an accessible landmark and has no counterpart in the compared frame.
relations.summary: While traveling with a maternal uncle, the user arranged to meet at an entrance near an elevator.

relations.reason: This independent reference-side preference is not addressed by any compared-side application or identity-document memory.
relations.summary: The user's maternal uncle prefers an aisle seat that makes standing easier during long-distance travel.

relations.reason: This reference-only epistemic limitation concerns current accessibility operations, a separate subject from the compared frame's document-validity limitation.
relations.summary: Past route records alone cannot establish whether an accessible entrance is operating on a particular day.

relations.reason: This compared-only timing fact is not supplied by the reference frame's statement about storage of document copies.
relations.summary: One identity document required renewal during the second half of 2025.

relations.reason: The compared memories form one before-and-after account of exact-name verification on official forms; the reference frame contains no form-entry claim.
relations.summary: An abbreviated name caused a mismatch with supporting documentation, while later source-document comparison avoided a correction request.

relations.reason: These compared memories split one scheduling lesson about jointly managing submission and issuance timing; the reference frame contains no application-calendar policy.
relations.summary: Tracking only a submission deadline led to a missed application deadline, while later practice separately recorded and verified submission and expected issuance dates.

relations.reason: This compared-only service-counter requirement is operationally independent from securely storing copies and has no reference-side counterpart.
relations.summary: Public-service staff expect identity-verification requesters to bring both an original document and a copy.

relations.reason: This compared-only epistemic limitation concerns document validity and is distinct from the reference frame's limitation concerning accessible-entrance operations.
relations.summary: A local agent cannot determine an identity document's current validity without its expiration date.

reports.both: Both frames support keeping identity-document copies consolidated, with the reference also specifying encrypted storage.
reports.compared_only: The compared frame covers renewal timing, exact name matching, deadline and issuance-date tracking, original-document requirements, and the information needed to assess current validity.
reports.reference_only: The reference describes transfer burdens, direct-route seating, weather exposure, accessible-entrance navigation and planning, travel arrangements with an uncle, his seating preference, and limits of historical accessibility records.
